title: King Oliver's pyorrhea and the origin of the qua-qua mute
summary: Oliver's bad teeth often kept him from playing; he got his mute sounds with his hand, and Paddy Harmon had someone copy it and sold a similar 'qua-qua' mute without paying Oliver.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I think in Stanley Dance's book he mentions that you said that King Oliver was having problems, too.

Well, King Oliver, he had pyorrhea real bad, and in those days, I mean, they didn't treat pyorrhea like they do now, you know. A lot of times the poor man was suffering so bad he couldn't even blow his horn and his teeth would hit the roof of his mouth half of the time, they were so weak.
Is it true that King Oliver originated the mute for trumpet?
With a bottle? is That right Do you know?

No, with his hand. He did all those things with his hand, and this fellow Harmon, Paddy Harmon, he sent -- he had a big ballroom and lots of money -- and he sent some guy to watch him to see how he was doing it. Then he invented a mute that he could make a similar noise but not exactly the same but real close.
And they used to call it the "qua-qua" mute, and he made a lot of money off it. He got wealthy. He got more rich. And that's it.
Then King Oliver didn't ever profit from it?
No, but he could do most anything with his hand without a mute. He never used a mute.
